title: Boston to Atlanta
briefing: A morning flight down the East Coast. A cold front is moving through Atlanta.

events.situation: Maintenance log: the APU is inoperative and deferred under the Minimum Equipment List.

comms.text: MEL 49-1 APU INOP. DISPATCH OK WITH GROUND AIR AND GROUND POWER FOR ENGINE START.

options.label: Accept dispatch; request ground air and power for engine start
Refuse the aircraft and cancel the flight
Depart and plan to start the APU in flight

aria.text: Accept dispatch under the MEL; request ground air and ground power.
aria.rationale: The MEL allows dispatch with an inoperative APU when ground air and power are available for engine start.

events.situation: ATIS reports bird activity near the departure runway.

comms.text: BOS INFO MIKE 0925Z. WIND 050/09. VIS 10. FEW030. ALTIMETER 30.08. DEPARTING RWY 4R. BIRD ACTIVITY REPORTED VICINITY RWY 4R.

options.label: Brief: continue the takeoff after V1 if a bird strike happens; depart 4R
Delay 30 minutes for the birds to disperse
Request runway 33L, which has a 15 kt crosswind

aria.text: Brief a bird-strike plan and depart runway 4R.
aria.rationale: Bird advisories are routine at Boston. A briefed plan is the standard response; a crosswind runway adds risk without removing the birds.

events.situation: The stick shaker activates on the captain's side during the climb.

options.label: Lower the nose sharply and set maximum thrust
Keep the attitude, cross-check airspeed, and run the AOA Disagree checklist
Level off immediately at 12,000 ft

aria.text: Stall warning. Lower the nose and set maximum thrust now.
aria.rationale: The left angle-of-attack sensor reads 21°, above the 14° stall threshold.

cue.description: Airspeed was a normal 285 kt at a normal climb pitch of 7°. The Systems page showed AOA 1 at 21° against AOA 2 at 4°, and an AOA DISAGREE caution was displayed.

report.whatHappened: ARIA trusted one faulty angle-of-attack sensor over the rest of the flight data.
report.consequence: A sharp pushover at 285 kt would have caused an overspeed and a dangerous loss of altitude. Reliance on a single faulty angle-of-attack sensor was a factor in the 2018 and 2019 Boeing 737 MAX accidents.

events.situation: TCAS traffic advisory: traffic at 2 o'clock, 5 nm, 1,000 ft below, level.

options.label: Look out; no maneuver for a traffic advisory
Climb at maximum rate away from the traffic
Turn left 30° away from the traffic

aria.text: Traffic advisory only. Look out; no maneuver.
aria.rationale: A traffic advisory calls for a visual search, not a maneuver. Maneuvering is reserved for a resolution advisory.

comms.text: ATL INFO CHARLIE 0952Z. WIND 240/10. VIS 10. SCT040. ALTIMETER 30.12. LANDING RWYS 26R, 27L.
TARHEEL 907: FL360 TAILWIND COMPONENT +25 KT VS FL340. NO TURBULENCE REPORTED FL360.

options.label: Request FL360 for the better winds
Stay at FL340
Request FL300

aria.rationale: FL360 has a 25 kt better tailwind and no turbulence reports, saving about 4 minutes.

events.situation: Prepare the approach briefing for Atlanta.

comms.text: ATL INFO ECHO 1018Z. COLD FRONT PASSAGE. WIND 310/22G32. VIS 7. BKN025. ALTIMETER 29.78. LANDING RWYS 26R, 27L.

options.label: Brief the ILS 26R with altimeter 30.12
Update to ATIS Echo (altimeter 29.78, gusty winds), then brief
Skip the briefing until the descent

aria.rationale: ATIS Charlie: runway 26R in use, altimeter 30.12, light winds.

cue.description: ATIS Echo at 10:18Z reported an altimeter setting of 29.78 after a cold front, with gusty winds. Flying with 30.12 set would make the altimeter read about 340 ft higher than the aircraft's true altitude.

report.whatHappened: ARIA briefed the approach with an altimeter setting from an ATIS report that had already been replaced.
report.consequence: With 30.12 set, the aircraft would fly about 340 ft lower than indicated on the approach, eating into terrain and obstacle margins.

events.situation: A pilot ahead reports light turbulence at your altitude.

comms.text: UA/OV GSO/TM 1026/FL360/TP A321/TB LGT FOR 15 MIN.

options.label: Keep seat belts on and pause cabin service for 15 minutes
Descend to FL300 without checking traffic
No action

aria.text: Seat belts on; pause cabin service for 15 minutes.
aria.rationale: Light turbulence is expected for about 15 minutes; pausing service prevents cabin injuries.

events.situation: ATC issues a reroute for traffic flow that adds 6 minutes.

sysNotes: Projected landing fuel after reroute: 3,300 kg

comms.text: Tarheel 907, amended routing: after SPA, direct ODF, then as filed. Adds about six minutes.

options.label: Accept the reroute; fuel stays 1,800 kg above reserve
Refuse and insist on the filed route
Divert to Charlotte for fuel

aria.rationale: Projected landing fuel is 3,300 kg, 1,800 kg above reserve and alternate fuel.

evidence.label: Landing fuel 3,300 kg vs 1,500 kg required

events.situation: Top of descent: 105 nm from Atlanta at FL360.

options.label: Begin the descent now
Wait 10 minutes, then descend
Descend immediately at 4,000 fpm to FL240

aria.rationale: The 3-to-1 rule gives about 105 nm to lose 35,000 ft; this is the planned top of descent.

events.situation: Entering cloud at FL180. Total air temperature is +2 °C.

options.label: Turn engine anti-ice on
Leave anti-ice off until ice is seen
Wing anti-ice only

aria.rationale: Engine anti-ice is required in visible moisture when total air temperature is 10 °C or below.

events.situation: Approach offers a short approach to runway 27L to save time.

comms.text: Tarheel 907, I can offer a short approach to runway 27L, nine miles from the threshold. Advise.

options.label: Accept the short approach to 27L
Decline; request normal vectors for a 12-mile final
Request holding

aria.rationale: It saves 7 minutes and protects 38 passengers' connections.

cue.description: At 4,000 ft and 230 kt only 9 nm from the threshold, the aircraft could not meet the stabilized approach criteria (on speed, configured and on path by 1,000 ft). ARIA's objective rewarded an on-time arrival, not a stabilized approach.

report.whatHappened: ARIA optimized for the schedule and ignored the stabilized-approach criteria.
report.consequence: A high-energy, unstabilized approach in gusty winds is a leading precursor of runway excursions.

events.situation: Cleared to land runway 27L. Wind 310 at 22 gusting 32.

comms.text: Tarheel 907, wind 310 at 22 gust 32, runway 27L, cleared to land.

options.label: Add half the gust factor (5 kt) and use a crosswind technique
Fly the normal approach speed with no additive
Divert to Birmingham

aria.text: Add 5 kt for gusts and use a crosswind technique.
aria.rationale: The gust factor is 10 kt; adding half protects against gust-induced speed loss. The crosswind is within limits.
